docs.title: 4. LRU Cache
docs.text:
Requirements: fixed capacity; get and put in O(1); evict the least recently used entry; thread-safe. Design: HashMap<K, Node> + doubly linked list with sentinel head/tail; a lock around both.

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

flowchart LR H[head sentinel] <--> A["MANGO (MRU)"] <--> B[MILK] <--> C["RICE (LRU)"] <--> T[tail sentinel] M[(HashMap key → node)] -.-> A M -.-> B M -.-> C LruCache.javaLruCacheDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.lrucache;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.StringJoiner;
import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;

/**
 * LRU cache with O(1) get and put: a HashMap for lookup plus a doubly linked list for recency
 * (most recent at the head). A single lock makes it thread-safe; shard it for high concurrency.
 */
public final class LruCache<K, V> {

    private static final class Node<K, V> {
        final K key;
        V value;
        Node<K, V> prev;
        Node<K, V> next;

        Node(K key, V value) {
            this.key = key;
            this.value = value;
        }
    }

    private final int capacity;
    private final Map<K, Node<K, V>> index = new HashMap<>();
    private final Node<K, V> head = new Node<>(null, null); // sentinels avoid null checks
    private final Node<K, V> tail = new Node<>(null, null);
    private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private int evictions;

    public LruCache(int capacity) {
        if (capacity < 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("capacity must be >= 1");
        }
        this.capacity = capacity;
        head.next = tail;
        tail.prev = head;
    }

    public V get(K key) {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            Node<K, V> n = index.get(key);
            if (n == null) {
                return null;
            }
            moveToHead(n);
            return n.value;
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    public void put(K key, V value) {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            Node<K, V> n = index.get(key);
            if (n != null) {
                n.value = value;
                moveToHead(n);
                return;
            }
            if (index.size() == capacity) {
                Node<K, V> lru = tail.prev;
                unlink(lru);
                index.remove(lru.key);
                evictions++;
            }
            n = new Node<>(key, value);
            index.put(key, n);
            linkAtHead(n);
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    private void moveToHead(Node<K, V> n) {
        unlink(n);
        linkAtHead(n);
    }

    private void unlink(Node<K, V> n) {
        n.prev.next = n.next;
        n.next.prev = n.prev;
    }

    private void linkAtHead(Node<K, V> n) {
        n.next = head.next;
        n.prev = head;
        head.next.prev = n;
        head.next = n;
    }

    public int evictions() {
        return evictions;
    }

    /** Most recently used first. */
    @Override
    public String toString() {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            StringJoiner j = new StringJoiner(", ", "[", "]");
            for (Node<K, V> n = head.next; n != tail; n = n.next) {
                j.add(n.key + "=" + n.value);
            }
            return j.toString();
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.lrucache;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;

public class LruCacheDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        var cache = new LruCache<String, String>(3);

        System.out.println("=== LLD: LRU cache (capacity 3) for product details ===");
        cache.put("MANGO", "Alphonso ₹399");
        cache.put("RICE", "Basmati ₹649");
        cache.put("MILK", "Toned ₹56");
        System.out.println("after 3 puts      : " + cache);
        System.out.println("get MANGO         : " + cache.get("MANGO"));
        System.out.println("order now         : " + cache);
        cache.put("BREAD", "Whole wheat ₹45");
        System.out.println("put BREAD (evicts least recently used RICE): " + cache);
        System.out.println("get RICE          : " + cache.get("RICE"));

        var shared = new LruCache<Integer, Integer>(100);
        CountDownLatch start = new CountDownLatch(1);
        List<Thread> threads = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; t++) {
            int offset = t * 1_000;
            threads.add(Thread.ofPlatform().start(() -> {
                try {
                    start.await();
                } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                }
                for (int i = 0; i < 1_000; i++) {
                    shared.put(offset + i, i);
                    shared.get(offset + i / 2);
                }
            }));
        }
        start.countDown();
        for (Thread t : threads) {
            t.join();
        }
        System.out.println("8 threads x 1,000 puts into capacity 100 -> evictions: " + shared.evictions()
                + " (exactly 8,000 - 100)");
    }
}

=== LLD: LRU cache (capacity 3) for product details ===
after 3 puts      : [MILK=Toned ₹56, RICE=Basmati ₹649, MANGO=Alphonso ₹399]
get MANGO         : Alphonso ₹399
order now         : [MANGO=Alphonso ₹399, MILK=Toned ₹56, RICE=Basmati ₹649]
put BREAD (evicts least recently used RICE): [BREAD=Whole wheat ₹45, MANGO=Alphonso ₹399, MILK=Toned ₹56]
get RICE          : null
8 threads x 1,000 puts into capacity 100 -> evictions: 7900 (exactly 8,000 - 100)

Follow-ups: the one-liner with LinkedHashMap(capacity, 0.75f, true) + removeEldestEntry; TTL expiry; LFU; sharding by key hash to reduce lock contention; Caffeine's W-TinyLFU in production.

docs.title: 5. Splitwise (Expense Sharing)
docs.text:
Requirements: groups of people; expenses paid by one person and split equally, by percentage or by exact amounts; show balances; settle up with few payments; never lose a paisa to rounding. Patterns: Strategy for split types; a greedy max-creditor/max-debtor settlement.

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

classDiagram class ExpenseSharing { +addExpense(paidBy, amount, participants, split) +balances() +settleUp() } class SplitStrategy { <<interface>> +split(amount, participants) Map } SplitStrategy <|.. Equal SplitStrategy <|.. Percent SplitStrategy <|.. Exact ExpenseSharing --> SplitStrategy ExpenseSharing.javaExpenseSharingDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.splitwise;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.PriorityQueue;
import java.util.TreeMap;

/**
 * Splitwise-style expense sharing. Patterns: Strategy (how an expense is split), and a greedy
 * "settle up" that minimises the number of payments by matching biggest creditor with biggest debtor.
 */
public final class ExpenseSharing {

    /** Strategy: who owes how much (in paise) of an amount. */
    public interface SplitStrategy {
        Map<String, Long> split(long amountPaise, List<String> participants);
    }

    public static SplitStrategy equal() {
        return (amount, people) -> {
            Map<String, Long> shares = new TreeMap<>();
            long base = amount / people.size();
            long remainder = amount % people.size();
            for (int i = 0; i < people.size(); i++) {
                shares.put(people.get(i), base + (i < remainder ? 1 : 0)); // spread leftover paise
            }
            return shares;
        };
    }

    public static SplitStrategy percent(Map<String, Integer> percents) {
        return (amount, people) -> {
            if (percents.values().stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum() != 100) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("percentages must add up to 100");
            }
            Map<String, Long> shares = new TreeMap<>();
            long assigned = 0;
            for (int i = 0; i < people.size(); i++) {
                String p = people.get(i);
                long share = i == people.size() - 1 ? amount - assigned : amount * percents.get(p) / 100;
                shares.put(p, share);
                assigned += share;
            }
            return shares;
        };
    }

    public static SplitStrategy exact(Map<String, Long> amounts) {
        return (amount, people) -> {
            if (amounts.values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum() != amount) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("exact shares must add up to the total");
            }
            return new TreeMap<>(amounts);
        };
    }

    private final Map<String, Long> balance = new TreeMap<>(); // + is owed money, - owes money

    public void addExpense(String paidBy, long amountPaise, List<String> participants, SplitStrategy split) {
        balance.merge(paidBy, amountPaise, Long::sum);
        split.split(amountPaise, participants).forEach((p, share) -> balance.merge(p, -share, Long::sum));
    }

    public Map<String, Long> balances() {
        return new TreeMap<>(balance);
    }

    /** Greedy settlement: at most n-1 payments. */
    public List<String> settleUp() {
        PriorityQueue<long[]> creditors = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Long.compare(b[1], a[1]));
        PriorityQueue<long[]> debtors = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> Long.compare(b[1], a[1]));
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(balance.keySet());
        for (int i = 0; i < names.size(); i++) {
            long b = balance.get(names.get(i));
            if (b > 0) {
                creditors.add(new long[] {i, b});
            } else if (b < 0) {
                debtors.add(new long[] {i, -b});
            }
        }
        List<String> payments = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!creditors.isEmpty() && !debtors.isEmpty()) {
            long[] c = creditors.poll();
            long[] d = debtors.poll();
            long amount = Math.min(c[1], d[1]);
            payments.add(String.format("%s pays %s ₹%,.2f", names.get((int) d[0]), names.get((int) c[0]), amount / 100.0));
            if (c[1] > amount) {
                creditors.add(new long[] {c[0], c[1] - amount});
            }
            if (d[1] > amount) {
                debtors.add(new long[] {d[0], d[1] - amount});
            }
        }
        return payments;
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.splitwise;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

public class ExpenseSharingDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var trip = new ExpenseSharing();
        List<String> all = List.of("Asha", "Ravi", "Meera", "Kabir");

        System.out.println("=== LLD: Splitwise-style expense sharing (Goa trip) ===");
        trip.addExpense("Asha", 1_200_000, all, ExpenseSharing.equal());                    // villa ₹12,000
        trip.addExpense("Ravi", 300_001, all, ExpenseSharing.equal());                      // dinner ₹3,000.01
        trip.addExpense("Meera", 400_000, List.of("Meera", "Kabir"),
                ExpenseSharing.percent(Map.of("Meera", 25, "Kabir", 75)));                  // scooter ₹4,000
        trip.addExpense("Kabir", 150_000, List.of("Asha", "Kabir"),
                ExpenseSharing.exact(Map.of("Asha", 100_000L, "Kabir", 50_000L)));          // shopping ₹1,500

        trip.balances().forEach((who, b) -> System.out.printf("%-6s %s ₹%,.2f%n", who, b >= 0 ? "gets back" : "owes     ",
                Math.abs(b) / 100.0));
        System.out.println("Sum of balances: " + trip.balances().values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum() + " paise");
        System.out.println("Settle up with the fewest payments:");
        trip.settleUp().forEach(p -> System.out.println("  " + p));
    }
}

=== LLD: Splitwise-style expense sharing (Goa trip) ===
Asha   gets back ₹7,249.99
Kabir  owes      ₹5,750.00
Meera  owes      ₹750.00
Ravi   owes      ₹749.99
Sum of balances: 0 paise
Settle up with the fewest payments:
  Kabir pays Asha ₹5,750.00
  Meera pays Asha ₹750.00
  Ravi pays Asha ₹749.99

Follow-ups: money as long paise (never double), the remainder-paise rule, multiple currencies, groups and expense history, and that the true minimum number of transactions is NP-hard (greedy is the practical answer).

docs.title: 6. Snake and Ladder
docs.text:
Requirements: configurable board; snakes go down, ladders go up; players take turns; exact roll needed to finish; first to the last square wins. Patterns: Builder with validation, Strategy for dice (seeded/fixed in tests).

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

SnakeAndLadder.javaSnakeAndLadderDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.snakeladder;

import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.Deque;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.IntSupplier;

/**
 * Snake and ladder LLD. Patterns: Builder (board configuration with validation), Strategy (dice,
 * so tests can use a fixed sequence), and a queue of players for turns.
 */
public final class SnakeAndLadder {

    public static final class Board {
        final int size;
        final Map<Integer, Integer> jumps; // snake heads and ladder bottoms → destination

        private Board(int size, Map<Integer, Integer> jumps) {
            this.size = size;
            this.jumps = Map.copyOf(jumps);
        }

        public static Builder builder(int size) {
            return new Builder(size);
        }

        public static final class Builder {
            private final int size;
            private final Map<Integer, Integer> jumps = new HashMap<>();

            Builder(int size) {
                this.size = size;
            }

            public Builder snake(int head, int tail) {
                if (tail >= head) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("snake must go down: " + head + "->" + tail);
                }
                return jump(head, tail);
            }

            public Builder ladder(int bottom, int top) {
                if (top <= bottom) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("ladder must go up: " + bottom + "->" + top);
                }
                return jump(bottom, top);
            }

            private Builder jump(int from, int to) {
                if (from <= 1 || from >= size || to < 1 || to > size || jumps.containsKey(from)) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("invalid jump " + from + "->" + to);
                }
                jumps.put(from, to);
                return this;
            }

            public Board build() {
                return new Board(size, jumps);
            }
        }
    }

    private final Board board;
    private final IntSupplier dice;
    private final Deque<String> turns;
    private final Map<String, Integer> positions = new HashMap<>();

    public SnakeAndLadder(Board board, IntSupplier dice, List<String> players) {
        this.board = board;
        this.dice = dice;
        this.turns = new ArrayDeque<>(players);
        players.forEach(p -> positions.put(p, 0));
    }

    /** Plays one turn and returns a description; ends with "WINS" when someone reaches the last square. */
    public String playTurn() {
        String player = turns.poll();
        int roll = dice.getAsInt();
        int from = positions.get(player);
        int to = from + roll;
        String note = "";
        if (to > board.size) {
            to = from;
            note = " (needs exact roll)";
        } else if (board.jumps.containsKey(to)) {
            int dest = board.jumps.get(to);
            note = dest > to ? " ladder to " + dest : " snake to " + dest;
            to = dest;
        }
        positions.put(player, to);
        turns.addLast(player);
        return String.format("%-5s rolls %d: %2d -> %2d%s%s", player, roll, from, to, note,
                to == board.size ? "  WINS" : "");
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.snakeladder;

import com.handbook.lld.snakeladder.SnakeAndLadder.Board;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;

public class SnakeAndLadderDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Board board = Board.builder(30)
                .ladder(3, 22).ladder(5, 8).ladder(11, 26).ladder(20, 29)
                .snake(27, 1).snake(21, 9).snake(17, 4).snake(19, 7)
                .build();
        Random seeded = new Random(19);
        var game = new SnakeAndLadder(board, () -> 1 + seeded.nextInt(6), List.of("Asha", "Ravi"));

        System.out.println("=== LLD: Snake and ladder (30 squares, seeded dice) ===");
        for (int turn = 0; turn < 40; turn++) {
            String line = game.playTurn();
            System.out.println(line);
            if (line.endsWith("WINS")) {
                break;
            }
        }
        try {
            Board.builder(30).snake(5, 12);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            System.out.println("Builder validation: " + e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}

=== LLD: Snake and ladder (30 squares, seeded dice) ===
Asha  rolls 6:  0 ->  6
Ravi  rolls 3:  0 -> 22 ladder to 22
Asha  rolls 3:  6 ->  9
Ravi  rolls 1: 22 -> 23
Asha  rolls 5:  9 -> 14
Ravi  rolls 6: 23 -> 29
Asha  rolls 3: 14 ->  4 snake to 4
Ravi  rolls 4: 29 -> 29 (needs exact roll)
Asha  rolls 3:  4 ->  7
Ravi  rolls 5: 29 -> 29 (needs exact roll)
Asha  rolls 5:  7 -> 12
Ravi  rolls 1: 29 -> 30  WINS
Builder validation: snake must go down: 5->12

Follow-ups: multiple dice, "roll a 6 to start", extra turn on 6, crooked dice for testing, and preventing loops (a ladder ending on a snake head that leads back).

docs.title: 7. Library Management
docs.text:
Requirements: books with copies; members (students: 2 loans, 14 days; faculty: 5 loans, 30 days); reservations queue when no copy is free; fines for late returns by member type; notify the next member when a reserved book comes back. Patterns: Strategy (fine policy), Observer (notifications).

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

Library.javaLibraryDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.library;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.temporal.ChronoUnit;
import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Queue;
import java.util.function.BiConsumer;

/**
 * Library management LLD. Patterns: Strategy (fine policy per member type), Observer (notify the
 * next member in the reservation queue when a copy is returned).
 */
public final class Library {

    public enum MemberType { STUDENT, FACULTY }

    public record Member(String id, String name, MemberType type) {
    }

    public record Loan(String isbn, Member member, LocalDate due) {
    }

    public interface FinePolicy {
        long finePaise(Member member, long daysLate);
    }

    /** Students: ₹5/day capped at ₹200; faculty: no fines for the first 7 late days, then ₹10/day. */
    public static FinePolicy standardFines() {
        return (m, days) -> switch (m.type()) {
            case STUDENT -> Math.min(days * 500, 20_000);
            case FACULTY -> Math.max(0, days - 7) * 1_000;
        };
    }

    private final Map<String, String> titles = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Integer> available = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Queue<Member>> reservations = new HashMap<>();
    private final List<Loan> loans = new ArrayList<>();
    private final FinePolicy fines;
    private final BiConsumer<Member, String> notifier; // Observer callback (SMS/e-mail in real life)

    public Library(FinePolicy fines, BiConsumer<Member, String> notifier) {
        this.fines = fines;
        this.notifier = notifier;
    }

    public void addBook(String isbn, String title, int copies) {
        titles.put(isbn, title);
        available.merge(isbn, copies, Integer::sum);
    }

    public String borrow(Member m, String isbn, LocalDate today) {
        if (loans.stream().filter(l -> l.member().equals(m)).count() >= (m.type() == MemberType.STUDENT ? 2 : 5)) {
            return m.name() + ": loan limit reached";
        }
        Queue<Member> queue = reservations.computeIfAbsent(isbn, k -> new ArrayDeque<>());
        if (available.getOrDefault(isbn, 0) == 0) {
            if (!queue.contains(m)) {
                queue.add(m);
            }
            return m.name() + ": no copies, reservation queue position " + (List.copyOf(queue).indexOf(m) + 1);
        }
        if (!queue.isEmpty() && !queue.peek().equals(m)) {
            return m.name() + ": " + titles.get(isbn) + " is reserved for " + queue.peek().name();
        }
        queue.poll();
        available.merge(isbn, -1, Integer::sum);
        LocalDate due = today.plusDays(m.type() == MemberType.STUDENT ? 14 : 30);
        loans.add(new Loan(isbn, m, due));
        return m.name() + " borrowed " + titles.get(isbn) + ", due " + due;
    }

    public String giveBack(Member m, String isbn, LocalDate today) {
        Loan loan = loans.stream().filter(l -> l.member().equals(m) && l.isbn().equals(isbn)).findFirst().orElseThrow();
        loans.remove(loan);
        available.merge(isbn, 1, Integer::sum);
        long late = Math.max(0, ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(loan.due(), today));
        long fine = fines.finePaise(m, late);
        Queue<Member> queue = reservations.get(isbn);
        if (queue != null && !queue.isEmpty()) {
            notifier.accept(queue.peek(), titles.get(isbn) + " is ready for pickup");
        }
        return m.name() + " returned " + titles.get(isbn) + (late > 0 ? ", " + late + " days late, fine ₹" + fine / 100 : ", on time");
    }
}

        var library = new Library(Library.standardFines(),
                (member, message) -> System.out.println("    notify " + member.name() + ": " + message));

docs.title: 8. Movie Ticket Booking
docs.text:
Requirements: a show's seat map; users select several seats; seats are held for 5 minutes while paying; all-or-nothing holds; confirm only while the hold is valid; expired holds become available; no double booking under concurrency. This is the core of BookMyShow-style designs.

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Free Free --> Held: hold (all requested seats free) Held --> Booked: confirm before expiry Held --> Free: hold expires Booked --> [*] ShowBooking.javaShowBookingDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.moviebooking;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;

/**
 * Movie ticket booking (BookMyShow-style) LLD. Core problem: two people must never get the same
 * seat. Seats are HELD for a few minutes while the user pays, then CONFIRMED or released.
 * Holds are atomic per seat (ConcurrentHashMap.compute); expired holds are reclaimable.
 */
public final class ShowBooking {

    public enum Status { HELD, BOOKED }

    public record SeatState(Status status, String user, Instant holdExpires) {
    }

    private final Map<String, SeatState> seats = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final List<String> layout;
    private final Duration holdTime;

    public ShowBooking(List<String> layout, Duration holdTime) {
        this.layout = List.copyOf(layout);
        this.holdTime = holdTime;
    }

    /** Hold all requested seats or none (seats are always processed in sorted order to avoid deadlock-like partial holds). */
    public synchronized boolean hold(String user, List<String> wanted, Instant now) {
        for (String seat : wanted) {
            if (!layout.contains(seat) || !isFree(seat, now)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        wanted.stream().sorted().forEach(seat -> seats.put(seat, new SeatState(Status.HELD, user, now.plus(holdTime))));
        return true;
    }

    public synchronized boolean confirm(String user, List<String> held, Instant now) {
        for (String seat : held) {
            SeatState s = seats.get(seat);
            if (s == null || s.status() != Status.HELD || !s.user().equals(user) || !now.isBefore(s.holdExpires())) {
                return false; // hold lost (expired or never ours): payment must be refunded
            }
        }
        held.forEach(seat -> seats.put(seat, new SeatState(Status.BOOKED, user, null)));
        return true;
    }

    private boolean isFree(String seat, Instant now) {
        SeatState s = seats.get(seat);
        return s == null || (s.status() == Status.HELD && !now.isBefore(s.holdExpires()));
    }

    public synchronized String seatMap(Instant now) {
        Map<String, String> view = new TreeMap<>();
        for (String seat : layout) {
            SeatState s = seats.get(seat);
            view.put(seat, s == null || isFree(seat, now) ? "." : s.status() == Status.BOOKED ? "X" : "h");
        }
        return view.toString();
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.moviebooking;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

public class ShowBookingDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException {
        var show = new ShowBooking(List.of("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4"), Duration.ofMinutes(5));
        Instant t = Instant.parse("2026-10-14T18:00:00Z");

        System.out.println("=== LLD: Movie ticket booking with seat holds ===");
        System.out.println("Asha holds A1,A2   : " + show.hold("asha", List.of("A1", "A2"), t));
        System.out.println("Ravi holds A2,A3   : " + show.hold("ravi", List.of("A2", "A3"), t) + " (all-or-nothing)");
        System.out.println("Ravi holds A3      : " + show.hold("ravi", List.of("A3"), t));
        System.out.println("seat map           : " + show.seatMap(t) + "  (h = held, X = booked)");
        System.out.println("Asha pays at +2 min: " + show.confirm("asha", List.of("A1", "A2"), t.plusSeconds(120)));
        System.out.println("Ravi pays at +6 min: " + show.confirm("ravi", List.of("A3"), t.plusSeconds(360)) + " (hold expired, refund)");
        System.out.println("seat map at +6 min : " + show.seatMap(t.plusSeconds(360)));

        var race = new ShowBooking(List.of("B7"), Duration.ofMinutes(5));
        AtomicInteger winners = new AtomicInteger();
        CountDownLatch start = new CountDownLatch(1);
        Thread[] users = new Thread[50];
        for (int i = 0; i < users.length; i++) {
            String user = "user-" + i;
            users[i] = Thread.ofVirtual().start(() -> {
                try {
                    start.await();
                } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                }
                if (race.hold(user, List.of("B7"), t)) {
                    winners.incrementAndGet();
                }
            });
        }
        start.countDown();
        for (Thread u : users) {
            u.join();
        }
        System.out.println("50 users race for seat B7 -> holds granted: " + winners.get());
    }
}

Ravi holds A2,A3   : false (all-or-nothing)
Ravi holds A3      : true
seat map           : {A1=h, A2=h, A3=h, A4=.}  (h = held, X = booked)
Asha pays at +2 min: true
Ravi pays at +6 min: false (hold expired, refund)
seat map at +6 min : {A1=X, A2=X, A3=., A4=.}
50 users race for seat B7 -> holds granted: 1

Follow-ups: in a distributed system, holds go into the database with UPDATE seats SET status='HELD', held_until=? WHERE id IN (...) AND (status='FREE' OR held_until < now()) and check the affected row count (or Redis SET NX EX per seat); payment and booking form a small saga; refunds for lost holds must be idempotent.

docs.title: 9. Notification System
docs.text:
Requirements: send order updates by email, SMS and push; respect user preferences; templates with per-channel formatting (SMS length limits); retry transient failures; one failing channel must not block the others. Patterns: Strategy (sender per channel), Factory/registry, Template Method (message skeleton), Decorator (retry).

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

classDiagram class NotificationService { +register(channel, sender) +notify(user, template, data) } class Sender { <<interface>> +send(user, text) } class MessageTemplate { <<abstract>> +render(user, data) #body(data) #format(text) } class RetryDecorator Sender <|.. RetryDecorator RetryDecorator --> Sender : wraps NotificationService --> Sender NotificationService --> MessageTemplate NotificationService.javaNotificationDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.notification;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.EnumMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Notification system LLD. Patterns: Strategy (one sender per channel), Factory/registry (channel →
 * sender), Template Method (every message renders the same way with channel-specific formatting),
 * Decorator (retry around any sender), and user preferences as data.
 */
public final class NotificationService {

    public enum Channel { EMAIL, SMS, PUSH }

    public record User(String id, String name, String email, String phone, Set<Channel> optedIn) {
    }

    /** Strategy. */
    public interface Sender {
        void send(User user, String text);
    }

    /** Template Method: fixed steps, channel-specific formatting hook. */
    public abstract static class MessageTemplate {
        public final String render(User user, Map<String, String> data) {
            return format(greeting(user) + body(data)); // the skeleton never changes
        }

        protected String greeting(User user) {
            return "Hi " + user.name() + ", ";
        }

        protected abstract String body(Map<String, String> data);

        protected String format(String text) {
            return text;
        }
    }

    /** Decorator: retries any sender a few times on failure. */
    public static Sender withRetry(Sender inner, int attempts, List<String> log) {
        return (user, text) -> {
            for (int i = 1; ; i++) {
                try {
                    inner.send(user, text);
                    return;
                } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                    log.add("retry " + i + " after: " + e.getMessage());
                    if (i == attempts) {
                        throw e;
                    }
                }
            }
        };
    }

    private final Map<Channel, Sender> senders = new EnumMap<>(Channel.class);
    private final List<String> failures = new ArrayList<>();

    public NotificationService register(Channel channel, Sender sender) {
        senders.put(channel, sender);
        return this;
    }

    public void notify(User user, MessageTemplate template, Map<String, String> data) {
        String text = template.render(user, data);
        for (Channel c : Channel.values()) {
            if (!user.optedIn().contains(c)) {
                continue; // respect preferences
            }
            try {
                senders.get(c).send(user, c == Channel.SMS && text.length() > 60 ? text.substring(0, 57) + "..." : text);
            } catch (RuntimeException e) {
                failures.add(c + " to " + user.id() + " failed: " + e.getMessage()); // one channel failing doesn't stop others
            }
        }
    }

    public List<String> failures() {
        return List.copyOf(failures);
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.notification;

import com.handbook.lld.notification.NotificationService.Channel;
import com.handbook.lld.notification.NotificationService.MessageTemplate;
import com.handbook.lld.notification.NotificationService.User;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

public class NotificationDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<String> retryLog = new ArrayList<>();
        int[] smsGatewayBlips = {1};
        var service = new NotificationService()
                .register(Channel.EMAIL, (u, text) -> System.out.println("  EMAIL to " + u.email() + ": " + text))
                .register(Channel.SMS, NotificationService.withRetry((u, text) -> {
                    if (smsGatewayBlips[0]-- > 0) {
                        throw new IllegalStateException("SMS gateway 503");
                    }
                    System.out.println("  SMS   to " + u.phone() + ": " + text);
                }, 3, retryLog))
                .register(Channel.PUSH, (u, text) -> {
                    throw new IllegalStateException("device token expired");
                });

        MessageTemplate outForDelivery = new MessageTemplate() {
            @Override
            protected String body(Map<String, String> d) {
                return "order " + d.get("order") + " is out for delivery with " + d.get("rider") + ", arriving by " + d.get("eta") + ".";
            }
        };

        System.out.println("=== LLD: Notification system ===");
        User asha = new User("U1", "Asha", "asha@example.com", "+91-98450-11111", Set.of(Channel.EMAIL, Channel.SMS, Channel.PUSH));
        User ravi = new User("U2", "Ravi", "ravi@example.com", "+91-98450-22222", Set.of(Channel.EMAIL));
        Map<String, String> data = Map.of("order", "ORD-9", "rider", "Imran", "eta", "18:30");
        service.notify(asha, outForDelivery, data);
        service.notify(ravi, outForDelivery, data);
        System.out.println("retry log: " + retryLog);
        System.out.println("failures : " + service.failures());
    }
}

Follow-ups: async delivery via a queue, dedupe keys (Idempotent Consumer), per-user rate limits, quiet hours, localization, delivery receipts, and provider failover.

docs.title: 10. Logging Framework
docs.text:
Requirements: levels DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR; named loggers in a hierarchy (com.shop.payment inherits from com.shop); multiple appenders with their own thresholds and formats (console, JSON file, pager); cheap when a level is disabled. Patterns: Chain of Responsibility, Strategy (formatter).

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

MiniLogger.javaLoggingDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.logging;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.function.Consumer;

/**
 * Logging framework LLD. Patterns: Chain of Responsibility (each appender handles the record if its
 * level allows, then passes it on), Strategy (formatter), and a hierarchy of named loggers
 * ("com.shop.payment" inherits settings from "com.shop" unless overridden).
 */
public final class MiniLogger {

    public enum Level { DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR }

    public record LogRecord(long epochMillis, Level level, String logger, String message) {
    }

    /** Strategy for turning a record into text. */
    public interface Formatter {
        String format(LogRecord r);
    }

    /** A link in the chain. */
    public static final class Appender {
        private final String name;
        private final Level threshold;
        private final Formatter formatter;
        private final Consumer<String> sink;
        private Appender next;

        public Appender(String name, Level threshold, Formatter formatter, Consumer<String> sink) {
            this.name = name;
            this.threshold = threshold;
            this.formatter = formatter;
            this.sink = sink;
        }

        public Appender then(Appender next) {
            this.next = next;
            return next;
        }

        void handle(LogRecord r) {
            if (r.level().compareTo(threshold) >= 0) {
                sink.accept("[" + name + "] " + formatter.format(r));
            }
            if (next != null) {
                next.handle(r);
            }
        }
    }

    private final Clock clock;
    private final Appender chain;
    private final Map<String, Level> levels = new TreeMap<>();

    public MiniLogger(Clock clock, Appender chain, Level rootLevel) {
        this.clock = clock;
        this.chain = chain;
        levels.put("", rootLevel);
    }

    public void setLevel(String loggerName, Level level) {
        levels.put(loggerName, level);
    }

    /** The most specific configured prefix wins: com.shop.payment → com.shop → root. */
    Level effectiveLevel(String loggerName) {
        String name = loggerName;
        while (true) {
            Level l = levels.get(name);
            if (l != null) {
                return l;
            }
            int dot = name.lastIndexOf('.');
            name = dot < 0 ? "" : name.substring(0, dot);
        }
    }

    public void log(String loggerName, Level level, String message) {
        if (level.compareTo(effectiveLevel(loggerName)) < 0) {
            return; // cheap early exit: no record, no formatting
        }
        chain.handle(new LogRecord(clock.millis(), level, loggerName, message));
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.logging;

import com.handbook.lld.logging.MiniLogger.Appender;
import com.handbook.lld.logging.MiniLogger.Level;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public class LoggingDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Clock clock = Clock.fixed(Instant.parse("2026-10-14T10:15:30Z"), ZoneOffset.UTC);
        List<String> alertsSent = new ArrayList<>();

        Appender console = new Appender("console", Level.DEBUG,
                r -> Instant.ofEpochMilli(r.epochMillis()).toString().substring(11, 19) + " " + r.level() + " " + r.logger() + " - " + r.message(),
                System.out::println);
        Appender json = new Appender("file", Level.INFO,
                r -> "{\"level\":\"" + r.level() + "\",\"logger\":\"" + r.logger() + "\",\"msg\":\"" + r.message() + "\"}",
                System.out::println);
        Appender pager = new Appender("pager", Level.ERROR, r -> r.logger() + ": " + r.message(), alertsSent::add);
        console.then(json).then(pager);

        var logger = new MiniLogger(clock, console, Level.INFO);
        logger.setLevel("com.shop.payment", Level.DEBUG);

        System.out.println("=== LLD: Logging framework (chain of appenders, logger hierarchy) ===");
        logger.log("com.shop.cart", Level.DEBUG, "cart recalculated");      // below INFO for com.shop: dropped
        logger.log("com.shop.cart", Level.INFO, "item added MANGO-1KG");
        logger.log("com.shop.payment.upi", Level.DEBUG, "UPI intent created"); // inherits DEBUG from com.shop.payment
        logger.log("com.shop.payment", Level.ERROR, "PayFast timeout for ORD-9");
        System.out.println("pages sent to on-call: " + alertsSent);
    }
}

docs.title: 11. Grocery Discount Engine
docs.text:
Requirements: rules like "buy 2 get 1 free" on a SKU, "10% off dairy for Gold members", "₹150 off over ₹1,000", "5% off over ₹2,000"; some rules stack, while among exclusive coupons only the best applies; the total never goes negative; new rules without changing the engine. Patterns: Specification (eligibility), Strategy (discount calculation).

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

DiscountEngine.javaDiscountDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.discount;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.Predicate;
import java.util.function.ToLongFunction;

/**
 * Grocery discount engine LLD. Patterns: Specification (eligibility predicates that combine with
 * and/or), Strategy (how a rule computes its discount), and a policy for combining rules:
 * stackable rules all apply; among exclusive rules only the best one does.
 */
public final class DiscountEngine {

    public record Item(String sku, String category, int qty, long unitPaise) {
        long total() {
            return qty * unitPaise;
        }
    }

    public record Cart(String customerTier, List<Item> items) {
        long subtotal() {
            return items.stream().mapToLong(Item::total).sum();
        }
    }

    /** Specification: is the rule applicable to this cart? */
    public interface Spec extends Predicate<Cart> {
        default Spec and(Spec other) {
            return c -> test(c) && other.test(c);
        }

        static Spec subtotalAtLeast(long paise) {
            return c -> c.subtotal() >= paise;
        }

        static Spec tier(String tier) {
            return c -> c.customerTier().equals(tier);
        }

        static Spec contains(String sku) {
            return c -> c.items().stream().anyMatch(i -> i.sku().equals(sku));
        }
    }

    public record Rule(String name, Spec when, ToLongFunction<Cart> discount, boolean exclusive) {
    }

    public record Applied(String rule, long paise) {
    }

    /** Strategies for common rules. */
    public static ToLongFunction<Cart> percentOffCategory(String category, int percent) {
        return c -> c.items().stream().filter(i -> i.category().equals(category)).mapToLong(Item::total).sum() * percent / 100;
    }

    public static ToLongFunction<Cart> buyXGetYFree(String sku, int x, int y) {
        return c -> c.items().stream().filter(i -> i.sku().equals(sku))
                .mapToLong(i -> (long) (i.qty() / (x + y)) * y * i.unitPaise()).sum();
    }

    public static ToLongFunction<Cart> flat(long paise) {
        return c -> paise;
    }

    private final List<Rule> rules = new ArrayList<>();

    public DiscountEngine add(Rule rule) {
        rules.add(rule);
        return this;
    }

    public List<Applied> apply(Cart cart) {
        List<Applied> applied = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Rule r : rules) {
            if (!r.exclusive() && r.when().test(cart)) {
                long d = r.discount().applyAsLong(cart);
                if (d > 0) {
                    applied.add(new Applied(r.name(), d));
                }
            }
        }
        rules.stream().filter(Rule::exclusive).filter(r -> r.when().test(cart))
                .map(r -> new Applied(r.name(), r.discount().applyAsLong(cart)))
                .filter(a -> a.paise() > 0)
                .max(Comparator.comparingLong(Applied::paise))
                .ifPresent(applied::add); // best exclusive offer only
        return applied;
    }

    public static Map<String, Long> summary(Cart cart, List<Applied> applied) {
        long discount = Math.min(cart.subtotal(), applied.stream().mapToLong(Applied::paise).sum()); // never negative totals
        return Map.of("subtotal", cart.subtotal(), "discount", discount, "total", cart.subtotal() - discount);
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.discount;

import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Cart;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Item;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Rule;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Spec;

import java.util.List;

public class DiscountDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var engine = new DiscountEngine()
                .add(new Rule("Mango 2+1 free", Spec.contains("MANGO-1KG"), DiscountEngine.buyXGetYFree("MANGO-1KG", 2, 1), false))
                .add(new Rule("Gold: 10% off dairy", Spec.tier("GOLD"), DiscountEngine.percentOffCategory("dairy", 10), false))
                .add(new Rule("FLAT150 over ₹1,000", Spec.subtotalAtLeast(100_000), DiscountEngine.flat(15_000), true))
                .add(new Rule("SAVE5% over ₹2,000", Spec.subtotalAtLeast(200_000),
                        c -> c.subtotal() * 5 / 100, true));

        System.out.println("=== LLD: Grocery discount engine ===");
        for (Cart cart : List.of(
                new Cart("GOLD", List.of(new Item("MANGO-1KG", "fruit", 3, 39_900), new Item("PANEER-200G", "dairy", 2, 9_000))),
                new Cart("REGULAR", List.of(new Item("RICE-5KG", "staples", 5, 64_900))),
                new Cart("REGULAR", List.of(new Item("MILK-1L", "dairy", 2, 5_600))))) {
            var applied = engine.apply(cart);
            System.out.printf("%s cart, subtotal ₹%,.2f%n", cart.customerTier(), cart.subtotal() / 100.0);
            applied.forEach(a -> System.out.printf("  - %-22s -₹%,.2f%n", a.rule(), a.paise() / 100.0));
            var s = DiscountEngine.summary(cart, applied);
            System.out.printf("  total ₹%,.2f%n", s.get("total") / 100.0);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 12. Tic-Tac-Toe
docs.text:
Requirements: n×n board; two players alternate; detect win or draw after each move in O(1); reject illegal moves and moves after the game ends.

Watch the design handle the demo scenario step by step, with the matching code lit up. Switch to Naive design to see a simpler design fail. Open in the explorer

TicTacToe.javaTicTacToeDemo.java 
package com.handbook.lld.tictactoe;

/**
 * Tic-tac-toe on an n×n board with O(1) win detection: keep a running sum per row, column and
 * diagonal (+1 for X, -1 for O). A line wins when its sum reaches ±n.
 */
public final class TicTacToe {

    public enum Result { IN_PROGRESS, X_WINS, O_WINS, DRAW }

    private final int n;
    private final char[][] cells;
    private final int[] rows;
    private final int[] cols;
    private int diagonal;
    private int antiDiagonal;
    private int moves;
    private char turn = 'X';
    private Result result = Result.IN_PROGRESS;

    public TicTacToe(int n) {
        this.n = n;
        this.cells = new char[n][n];
        this.rows = new int[n];
        this.cols = new int[n];
    }

    public Result move(int r, int c) {
        if (result != Result.IN_PROGRESS) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("game over: " + result);
        }
        if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= n || c >= n || cells[r][c] != 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("illegal move " + r + "," + c);
        }
        cells[r][c] = turn;
        int delta = turn == 'X' ? 1 : -1;
        rows[r] += delta;
        cols[c] += delta;
        if (r == c) {
            diagonal += delta;
        }
        if (r + c == n - 1) {
            antiDiagonal += delta;
        }
        moves++;
        if (Math.abs(rows[r]) == n || Math.abs(cols[c]) == n || Math.abs(diagonal) == n || Math.abs(antiDiagonal) == n) {
            result = turn == 'X' ? Result.X_WINS : Result.O_WINS;
        } else if (moves == n * n) {
            result = Result.DRAW;
        }
        turn = turn == 'X' ? 'O' : 'X';
        return result;
    }

    public String board() {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (char[] row : cells) {
            for (char cell : row) {
                sb.append(cell == 0 ? '.' : cell);
            }
            sb.append('\n');
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }
}

package com.handbook.lld.tictactoe;

public class TicTacToeDemo {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("=== LLD: Tic-tac-toe with O(1) win check ===");
        var game = new TicTacToe(3);
        int[][] moves = {{1, 1}, {0, 0}, {0, 2}, {2, 0}, {1, 0}, {1, 2}, {2, 2}, {0, 1}, {2, 1}};
        TicTacToe.Result result = null;
        for (int[] m : moves) {
            result = game.move(m[0], m[1]);
        }
        System.out.print(game.board());
        System.out.println("result: " + result);

        var quick = new TicTacToe(3);
        quick.move(0, 0);
        quick.move(1, 0);
        quick.move(1, 1);
        quick.move(2, 0);
        System.out.println("X plays 2,2 -> " + quick.move(2, 2) + " (main diagonal)");
        try {
            quick.move(0, 1);
        } catch (IllegalStateException e) {
            System.out.println("next move -> " + e.getMessage());
        }
    }
}

=== LLD: Tic-tac-toe with O(1) win check ===
OOX
XXO
OXX
result: DRAW
X plays 2,2 -> X_WINS (main diagonal)
next move -> game over: X_WINS

Follow-ups: k-in-a-row on larger boards (counters don't work directly; check around the last move), an AI player (minimax as a Strategy), undo (Command), and online multiplayer (server-authoritative state).

Unit Tests: LldProblemsTest.java 
package com.handbook.lld;

import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Cart;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Item;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Rule;
import com.handbook.lld.discount.DiscountEngine.Spec;
import com.handbook.lld.lrucache.LruCache;
import com.handbook.lld.moviebooking.ShowBooking;
import com.handbook.lld.parkinglot.ParkingLot;
import com.handbook.lld.parkinglot.ParkingLot.Vehicle;
import com.handbook.lld.parkinglot.ParkingLot.VehicleType;
import com.handbook.lld.splitwise.ExpenseSharing;
import com.handbook.lld.systemdesign.ConsistentHashRing;
import com.handbook.lld.tictactoe.TicTacToe;
import com.handbook.lld.vending.VendingMachine;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

class LldProblemsTest {

    private static final Instant T0 = Instant.parse("2026-01-01T00:00:00Z");

    @Test
    void parkingLotNeverPutsACarInASmallSpot() {
        var lot = new ParkingLot(ParkingLot.nearestSmallestFit(), (t, d) -> 0).addFloor(0, 2, 0, 0);
        assertThat(lot.park(new Vehicle("C", VehicleType.CAR), T0)).isEmpty();
        assertThat(lot.park(new Vehicle("B", VehicleType.BIKE), T0)).isPresent();
    }

    @Test
    void vendingMachineGivesCorrectChange() {
        var vm = new VendingMachine().load("A", new VendingMachine.Product("x", 13), 1);
        vm.insert(10);
        vm.insert(10);
        assertThat(vm.select("A")).endsWith("change [5, 2]");
    }

    @Test
    void lruEvictsLeastRecentlyUsed() {
        var c = new LruCache<String, Integer>(2);
        c.put("a", 1);
        c.put("b", 2);
        c.get("a");
        c.put("c", 3);
        assertThat(c.get("b")).isNull();
        assertThat(c.get("a")).isEqualTo(1);
    }

    @Test
    void expenseBalancesAlwaysSumToZero() {
        var s = new ExpenseSharing();
        s.addExpense("a", 1_001, List.of("a", "b", "c"), ExpenseSharing.equal());
        assertThat(s.balances().values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum()).isZero();
        assertThat(s.settleUp()).hasSize(2);
    }

    @Test
    void expiredHoldCanBeTakenByAnotherUser() {
        var show = new ShowBooking(List.of("A1"), Duration.ofMinutes(5));
        assertThat(show.hold("u1", List.of("A1"), T0)).isTrue();
        assertThat(show.hold("u2", List.of("A1"), T0.plusSeconds(60))).isFalse();
        assertThat(show.hold("u2", List.of("A1"), T0.plusSeconds(301))).isTrue();
        assertThat(show.confirm("u1", List.of("A1"), T0.plusSeconds(302))).isFalse();
    }

    @Test
    void onlyBestExclusiveDiscountApplies() {
        var engine = new DiscountEngine()
                .add(new Rule("a", Spec.subtotalAtLeast(0), DiscountEngine.flat(100), true))
                .add(new Rule("b", Spec.subtotalAtLeast(0), DiscountEngine.flat(300), true));
        var applied = engine.apply(new Cart("R", List.of(new Item("x", "c", 1, 1_000))));
        assertThat(applied).extracting(DiscountEngine.Applied::rule).containsExactly("b");
    }

    @Test
    void ticTacToeDetectsColumnWin() {
        var g = new TicTacToe(3);
        g.move(0, 0);
        g.move(0, 1);
        g.move(1, 0);
        g.move(1, 1);
        assertThat(g.move(2, 0)).isEqualTo(TicTacToe.Result.X_WINS);
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> g.move(2, 2)).isInstanceOf(IllegalStateException.class);
    }

    @Test
    void consistentHashingIsStable() {
        var ring = new ConsistentHashRing(50);
        ring.addNode("n1");
        ring.addNode("n2");
        String before = ring.nodeFor("k");
        assertThat(ring.nodeFor("k")).isEqualTo(before);
        assertThat(Map.of("n1", 1, "n2", 1)).containsKey(before);
    }
}

docs.title: Microsoft: Design Patterns in Interviews
docs.text:
Commonly reported, not official

Based on publicly shared candidate experiences and Microsoft's general interview guidance. Teams run their own loops, and formats vary by level and organization. Confirm with your recruiter.

docs.title: What the process commonly looks like
docs.text:
• A screening call or online assessment, then a loop of several interviews (often 4–5) with different engineers and a hiring manager.
  • Rounds mix coding, design (object-oriented design for mid-level, system design for senior), and behavioral questions about collaboration, growth mindset and customer focus.
  • Teams building developer platforms (Azure, Office, Windows, GitHub, Xbox) often ask domain-flavoured design questions.

docs.title: Where design patterns show up
docs.text:
Situation Pattern knowledge that helps "Design a class library / SDK" Builder, Factory Method, Facade, immutability, versioning OOD questions (parking lot, elevator, file system) State, Strategy, Composite, Observer Cloud service design Retry/Timeout/Bulkhead, Circuit Breaker, Config Server, Sidecar Productivity apps (editor, collaboration) Command (undo), Memento, Observer, Flyweight

Azure Architecture Center

Microsoft publishes a catalogue of cloud design patterns (Circuit Breaker, Retry, Bulkhead, Sidecar, Strangler Fig, CQRS, Event Sourcing, Gateway patterns and more). The microservices section of this handbook covers most of them with runnable code, and it's worth skimming Microsoft's descriptions before a loop.

docs.title: What interviewers look for
docs.text: Signal What strong looks like Problem solving & coding Correct, efficient, readable; tests edge cases Design Clear classes and responsibilities, extensibility where it's needed, trade-offs stated Collaboration Explains reasoning, accepts feedback, asks good questions Growth mindset Talks about learning from mistakes and feedback Customer focus Connects design choices to user impact

docs.title: 15 practice questions (with model answers)
docs.text:
1. Design a file system with folders and files that can compute total size.

Composite: Node interface with size(); Folder sums children. Add a Visitor for operations like search or permissions reports.

2. Implement undo/redo for a drawing app.

Command objects on undo/redo stacks; clear redo on new actions; group commands into macros; consider Memento for complex objects.

3. Design a parking lot.

Spot types via enum/factory, pricing Strategy, ticket lifecycle, concurrency on spot allocation. See the Parking Lot LLD.

4. How would you design an SDK client for a cloud storage service?

Builder for client configuration, immutable request objects, retries with backoff and jitter for transient errors, pluggable credentials (Strategy), pagination via Iterator, a Facade for common tasks.

5. Where would you use the Observer pattern in a collaborative document editor?

Views observing the document model; remote changes as events; batching updates to avoid UI storms; weak references or explicit unsubscription to avoid leaks.

6. Explain the Retry pattern. When can retrying make things worse?

Retry transient failures with backoff and jitter; it worsens outages when it multiplies load (retry storms) or duplicates non-idempotent operations. See Retry / Timeout / Bulkhead.

7. Design an elevator controller for a 20-floor building with 4 elevators.

State per elevator, a dispatching Strategy (nearest car, SCAN), requests queue, observers for displays. See the Elevator LLD.

8. What's the difference between Decorator and Proxy?

Both wrap the same interface. Decorator adds behavior (stackable); Proxy controls access (lazy loading, security, remote). See Comparisons.

9. How do you make a service's configuration changeable without redeploys?

Externalized config with refresh for flags/limits, typed validation, secrets in a vault, staged rollout. See Config Server.

10. Design a logging framework.

Levels with Chain of Responsibility or filters, appenders as Strategy, async appender with a bounded queue, formatter templates. See the Logging LLD.

11. How would you migrate a large legacy service to the cloud without downtime?

Strangler Fig behind a gateway, ACL for legacy data, gradual rollout with kill switches, parallel runs for calculations.

12. Explain the Sidecar pattern and give a use case.

A helper process next to the app (same pod) for cross-cutting concerns: mTLS, telemetry, log shipping, secrets. See Sidecar.

13. Why prefer composition over inheritance? Give an example.

Inheritance couples subclasses to parent internals and explodes combinations; composition (Strategy/Decorator) varies behavior at runtime. E.g. Notifier with pluggable channels instead of EmailSmsPushNotifier subclasses.

14. Design a thread pool.

Bounded work queue, worker threads, rejection policy, graceful shutdown, metrics; discuss sizing for CPU vs. I/O. See Thread Pool.

15. Tell me about a time you received critical feedback on a design.

STAR focused on listening, what you changed, and the outcome; Microsoft interviewers often probe for growth mindset.

docs.title: 4-week plan
docs.text:
Week Do 1 Coding fundamentals + OOP/SOLID; implement Composite, Command, Observer examples yourself 2 6 OOD problems from LLD problems in 45 minutes each; review with the class diagrams 3 Cloud patterns: retry, circuit breaker, sidecar, strangler, CQRS; one system design mock 4 Behavioral stories (growth mindset, collaboration, customer impact); mock loop

docs.title: Name That Pattern
docs.text:
A quick way to test yourself before an interview. Each question plays one of the handbook's animated walkthroughs with the names hidden: the boxes are just A, B, C. Watch what moves between them, then pick the pattern.

  • Scoring: 2 points for a right answer, 1 if you used Show the names first.
  • Hard mode hides the labels on the moving messages too, so you have only the shape of the conversation to go on.
  • Filter by family (Creational, Structural, Behavioral, Concurrency, Microservices, Architecture) to drill one area.
  • If you mix up a known look-alike pair, the answer explains how to tell them apart.

Use it like an interviewer would

Before you click an answer, say out loud what you see: who calls whom, what gets created, what is shared, what happens on failure. Interviewers grade that reasoning as much as the name.

Want to compare two patterns you keep confusing? See Pattern Comparisons, where look-alike pairs play side by side.

docs.title: Revision Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
One page to revise every pattern in the handbook the night before an interview. Each row: intent, the key mechanism, a real JDK/Spring example, and one sentence to say. Click a pattern name for the full page with three worked examples.

How to use this page

Cover the last column and try to say it yourself. If you can't explain a row in one breath, read that pattern's Quick Revision Card and Interview Corner.

docs.title: Creational
docs.text: Pattern Intent Key mechanism Real example Say this Singleton Exactly one instance Private constructor; enum / holder / DCL + volatile Runtime.getRuntime(); Spring singleton scope "Enum or holder idiom; DCL needs volatile; it's one per class loader, never per cluster." Factory Method Decide which class to create Static factory, overridden createX(), or a registry List.of, Calendar.getInstance, Collection.iterator() "Callers depend on an interface; new types need no edits; no silent default." Abstract Factory Create matching families One method per product, one factory per family DocumentBuilderFactory, Spring @Configuration + @Profile "Easy to add a family, hard to add a product type." Builder Assemble complex immutable objects Fluent builder, step builder, director StringBuilder, HttpRequest.newBuilder(), Thread.ofVirtual() "Fixes telescoping constructors; cross-field validation in build()." Prototype Create by copying Copy constructor / copy(); registry of templates new ArrayList<>(list), JsonNode.deepCopy() "Deep-copy mutable fields, share immutable ones; avoid clone()." Object Pool Reuse expensive, limited objects Bounded queue, validate on borrow, reset on return HikariCP, HTTP connection pools "Acquire late, release early; size with Little's Law; never pool cheap objects."

docs.title: Structural
docs.text: Pattern Intent Key mechanism Real example Say this Adapter Make an interface fit Wrap the adaptee; translate calls, data, errors Arrays.asList, InputStreamReader, Spring HandlerAdapter "Changes the interface; translate units and codes; fail loudly on unknowns." Bridge Two dimensions varying independently Abstraction holds an implementor JDBC API + drivers, SLF4J + back-ends "M + N classes instead of M × N; designed up front." Composite Treat parts and wholes alike Composite delegates to children and combines Swing Container, DOM, Spring Composite* "Uniform trees; watch cycles and deep recursion." Decorator Add behavior dynamically Same interface, wraps one object, stackable BufferedInputStream, Spring AOP "Same interface, adds behavior; order matters." Facade Simplify a subsystem Task-level methods orchestrate many classes JdbcTemplate, SLF4J, Spring @Service use cases "One simple entry point; avoid god facades." Flyweight Save memory by sharing Intrinsic (shared, immutable) vs extrinsic (passed in) Integer.valueOf cache, String pool "Integer 127 == 127 but 128 != 128; bound the pool." Proxy Control access Same interface; lazy, protection, remote, caching @Transactional, Hibernate lazy loading, gRPC stubs "Controls access vs Decorator adds behavior; self-invocation bypasses Spring proxies."

docs.title: Behavioral
docs.text: Pattern Intent Key mechanism Real example Say this Chain of Responsibility Pass a request along handlers Linked handlers or a list; may short-circuit Servlet FilterChain, Spring Security filters "Order is policy; make 'unhandled' explicit." Command Request as an object execute/undo; invoker keeps history or a queue Runnable, Swing Action, job queues "Queue, log, retry, undo; commands need IDs and idempotency." Interpreter Evaluate a small language Parser → AST of terminal/non-terminal nodes Regex, SpEL, JPQL, cron "Parse once, evaluate many; keep grammars small; never eval untrusted code." Iterator Traverse without exposing structure hasNext/next; lazy pagination, merging Collection.iterator(), ResultSet, AWS paginators "Fail-fast vs weakly consistent; k-way merge with a heap." Mediator Centralize peer coordination Colleagues talk only to the mediator DispatcherServlet, chat rooms, orchestrators "Many-to-many becomes many-to-one; beware the god mediator." Memento Snapshot and restore Originator creates opaque snapshots; caretaker stores Savepoints, Spring Batch ExecutionContext "Snapshot undo vs Command's inverse undo; version persisted mementos." Observer Notify dependents of changes Subscribe / notify; unsubscribe handles @EventListener, PropertyChangeListener, Kafka "Isolate failures, avoid leaks, notify after commit." State Behavior depends on state Context delegates; states return next state Order/payment lifecycles, Thread.State "States switch themselves; Strategy is chosen by the client." Strategy Swap algorithms Interface or lambda injected into a context Comparator, PasswordEncoder "Composition, runtime choice; lambdas make it one line." Template Method Fixed skeleton, variable steps final template + abstract steps + hooks HttpServlet.service, AbstractList, JdbcTemplate "Hollywood Principle; make the template final." Visitor Add operations to stable types Double dispatch, or sealed + pattern matching FileVisitor, compiler AST visitors "Easy new operations, hard new types; avoid no-op defaults." Null Object Replace null with neutral behavior Same interface, do-nothing implementation Collections.emptyList(), NOP loggers "Optional at boundaries, Null Object inside; never for security or payments." Specification Composable business rules isSatisfiedBy + and/or/not Spring Data JPA Specification "One definition of each rule; translate to SQL for big data."

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: Pattern Intent Key mechanism Real example Say this Producer-Consumer Decouple producers and consumers Bounded BlockingQueue, poison pills ThreadPoolExecutor, async log appenders, Kafka "Always bound the queue; while around wait()." Thread Pool Reuse a bounded set of threads Core → queue → max → rejection policy ThreadPoolExecutor, Tomcat pools "Explicit bounded queue; CPU-bound ≈ cores; beware same-pool deadlock." Future / Promise Result available later; compose async work supplyAsync, thenCompose, allOf, timeouts CompletableFuture, HttpClient.sendAsync "Always pass an executor for I/O; thenCompose is flatMap." Read-Write Lock Shared reads, exclusive writes ReentrantReadWriteLock, StampedLock Caches, configuration "Downgrade OK, upgrade deadlocks; no I/O under the write lock." Immutable Object Thread safety without locks Final fields, defensive copies, withers String, java.time, records "Records are shallowly immutable: List.copyOf components." Double-Checked Locking Lazy init with minimal locking Check, lock, check again; volatile Guava memoize, String.hashCode (racy single-check) "Without volatile you can see a half-built object." Virtual Threads Millions of cheap blocking threads JVM-scheduled, unmount on blocking Spring Boot spring.threads.virtual.enabled "I/O-bound only; limit resources, not threads; watch pinning."

docs.title: SOLID in five lines
docs.text: Principle One line Patterns that embody it Single Responsibility One reason to change Facade, Command, Strategy (one algorithm per class) Open/Closed Extend without modifying Strategy, Decorator, Observer, Factory, Visitor Liskov Substitution Subtypes must keep the parent's promises Template Method (hooks must not break the template) Interface Segregation Small, focused interfaces Role interfaces, Adapter targets Dependency Inversion Depend on abstractions Strategy, Abstract Factory, DI in general

docs.title: The 15 sentences interviewers most like to hear
docs.text:
1. "I'd introduce this pattern when the second variation appears; until then a simple if is clearer."
  2. "Strategy and State share a structure; the difference is who switches the behavior."
  3. "Decorator adds behavior, Proxy controls access, Adapter changes the interface, Facade simplifies."
  4. "Double-checked locking needs volatile to prevent publishing a partially constructed object."
  5. "Spring's @Transactional is a proxy, so self-invocation bypasses it."
  6. "Records are shallowly immutable; I copy mutable components in the compact constructor."
  7. "Every queue needs a bound and a decision about what happens when it's full."
  8. "Retries need idempotency keys; retrying a non-idempotent POST double-charges."
  9. "Virtual threads remove the thread limit, so I make resource limits explicit with pools and semaphores."
  10. "I never do I/O while holding a lock; I prepare outside and swap inside."
  11. "A singleton is per class loader / per JVM; across pods I need a database sequence or leader election."
  12. "Unknown codes and states should fail loudly, never fall into a silent default."
  13. "In-process events must be published after commit, or through an outbox across services."
  14. "For closed hierarchies in Java 21, sealed types + pattern matching give me Visitor's safety with less code."
  15. "Patterns are responses to forces. Let me first name the force, then pick the pattern."

docs.title: Night-before checklist
docs.text:
• I can write a thread-safe Singleton three ways (enum, holder, DCL with volatile).
  • I can write a Builder with validation in build() and explain step builders.
  • I can implement a Strategy with lambdas and explain Strategy vs State.
  • I can implement Observer with unsubscribe and failure isolation.
  • I can explain ThreadPoolExecutor task flow and rejection policies.
  • I can write a bounded buffer with wait/notifyAll or BlockingQueue.
  • I can explain Decorator vs Proxy vs Adapter vs Facade in one breath.
  • I can map patterns onto Parking Lot, Elevator, Vending Machine and Notification System designs (see the Pattern Selection Guide).
  • I have a STAR story for at least three patterns (see the end of each pattern page).

docs.title: SAP: Design Patterns in Interviews
docs.text:
Commonly reported, not official

Based on publicly shared candidate experiences. SAP is large (product teams, SAP Labs locations, cloud and on-premise products, consulting), and each unit interviews differently. Confirm with your recruiter.

docs.title: What the process commonly looks like
docs.text:
• An online test or screening (for early-career roles), followed by technical interviews and a managerial/HR conversation.
  • Java developer roles commonly cover core Java, OOP/design patterns, Spring Boot, REST, SQL, and increasingly cloud-native topics (microservices, Kubernetes, multi-tenancy).
  • Teams working on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) or extensions may discuss SAP-specific technologies such as the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP), which supports Java and Node.js, or integration with S/4HANA via APIs and events. Knowing the general patterns behind them (multi-tenancy, extensibility, events, ACLs) matters more than product trivia.
  • Experienced candidates are often asked about enterprise concerns: data consistency, extensibility, backward compatibility, security, and long product lifecycles.

docs.title: Where design patterns show up
docs.text: Situation Pattern knowledge that helps Enterprise application design Layered, Hexagonal, Clean, Modular Monolith Extensibility for customers/partners Strategy, Template Method (hooks), Observer/events, plugin Factory registries Integrating with ERP or legacy systems Anti-Corruption Layer, Adapter, Facade, Strangler Fig Multi-tenant SaaS Tenant routing (API Gateway), Rate Limiter, config per tenant, data isolation Business events Event-Driven, Outbox, Saga, Event Sourcing

docs.title: What interviewers look for
docs.text: Signal What strong looks like Java & Spring depth Collections, concurrency, JVM basics; Spring DI, transactions, proxies; JPA pitfalls Design Clean responsibilities, extensibility without hacks, backward compatibility awareness Enterprise thinking Data consistency, auditability, security, multi-tenancy, upgrades over many years Collaboration Working across global teams, documenting decisions, customer orientation

docs.title: 15 practice questions (with model answers)
docs.text:
1. How would you let customers add custom validation rules to an order process without changing core code?

Extension points: a ValidationRule Strategy interface registered per tenant, executed as a Chain; events for side effects; sandboxing and timeouts for customer code.

2. Explain how Spring's @Transactional works and when it doesn't.

A Proxy wraps the bean and starts/commits transactions; self-invocation bypasses the proxy, private methods aren't proxied, and checked exceptions don't roll back by default.

3. Design integration between a new cloud service and an existing ERP system.

ACL translating ERP data and codes; APIs for queries, events for changes; Outbox for reliable publishing; idempotent consumers; reconciliation jobs.

4. How would you design a multi-tenant SaaS application?

Tenant resolution at the gateway, tenant context propagated, isolation model (shared schema with tenant ID, schema per tenant, or DB per tenant), per-tenant config and limits, noisy-neighbour protection, tenant-aware monitoring.

5. Template Method vs. Strategy for extensibility?

Template Method fixes the algorithm skeleton with overridable hooks (inheritance); Strategy swaps whole behaviors via composition. Prefer Strategy for customer extensions. See Comparisons.

6. How do you evolve a public API used by thousands of customers?

Additive, backward-compatible changes; versioning for breaking changes; deprecation periods; consumer-driven contract tests; tolerant readers. See BFF (versioned partner contracts).

7. A business process spans finance, logistics and sales services. How do you keep data consistent?

Saga (orchestrated for core processes), Outbox, idempotency, semantic locks (PENDING states), and audit trails.

8. Where would you use Event Sourcing in an enterprise system?

Ledgers, approvals and workflows with strict audit needs; not for master data. Discuss snapshots, upcasting and GDPR (crypto-shredding). See Event Sourcing.

9. Explain the Adapter and Facade patterns with an integration example.

Adapter converts a legacy interface to the one you need; Facade gives a simple entry point over many calls (e.g. one createSalesOrder() hiding five BAPI-style calls).

10. How would you make a long-running batch job restartable?

Chunked processing with checkpoints (Spring Batch), idempotent writes, job state persisted, Command-like steps, and a dead-letter list for failed records.

11. How do you handle configuration and secrets across many landscapes (dev, test, prod)?

Externalized config per environment, typed validation, secrets in a vault/credential store, no secrets in code. See Config Server.

12. What is CQRS and when is it useful in enterprise apps?

Separate write models (rules) from read models (reports, dashboards); useful for heavy reporting or cross-module views. See CQRS.

13. How do you migrate a monolithic on-premise module to the cloud incrementally?

Strangler Fig: facade, extract capabilities one by one, ACL for remaining legacy data, parallel runs, retire old code.

14. How do you ensure a design stays maintainable over a 10-year product lifecycle?

Clear module boundaries, dependency rules enforced by tests (ArchUnit), documented decisions (ADRs), stable public APIs, and avoiding framework lock-in in the core (Clean).

15. Tell me about working with a distributed team across time zones.

STAR: communication practices (written design docs, async reviews), a concrete conflict or misunderstanding, and how you resolved it.

docs.title: 4-week plan
docs.text:
Week Do 1 Core Java + OOP/SOLID; creational and structural patterns; Spring proxies and transactions 2 Behavioral patterns with extensibility focus (Strategy, Template Method, Observer, Chain); 3 LLD problems 3 Architecture (layered, hexagonal, clean, modular monolith) and integration patterns (ACL, outbox, saga, CQRS) 4 Multi-tenancy and API evolution scenarios; STAR stories; mock interviews
